title: How long ago did the group start, and how far could a person walk?
description: A group walked about four hundred kilometres to reach a place. We assume how far they walk in a day to find when they started, then assume a lifetime of non-stop walking to count the rounds of the Earth. Keeko doubts a daily distance that leaves out the hours.
teaching_notes: One idea: state each assumption, then multiply the rates one step at a time. Watch for students who use the distance for one hour as if it were the distance for a whole day.

source: A group walked about 400 km; how many times can a person walk around the Earth in a lifetime
video_script.why: Questions without all the numbers are solved by stating sensible assumptions and then combining the rates one step at a time.
video_script.substitution: Assume a distance for one hour or one day, then multiply or divide in single steps.
video_script.anchor: a long walk of about 400 km, and a lifetime of walking round the Earth
video_script.wrong_answer: about three times around the Earth
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko uses 5 km for a whole day, so 5 × 365 × 70 = 127750 km, about 3 times around. But 5 km is the distance for one hour; a day has 24 hours, so a day gives 5 × 24 = 120 km.
video_script.payoff_line: State each assumption, then multiply the rates one step at a time

final_answer.value: About 16 days ago; about 76 times around the Earth
final_answer.spoken: The group started about sixteen days ago. A person could walk around the Earth about seventy six times.

names.Laksh: one of the two children who overhear the group
names.Ruhee: one of the two children who overhear the group

maths_rules: assume the group walked 25 km in a day: 400 ÷ 25 = 16 days
assume 5 km in each hour, non-stop: 5 × 24 = 120 km a day
the distance around the Earth is 40000 km: 3066000 ÷ 40000 = 76.65, so about 76 full times
the slip: 5 × 365 × 70 = 127750 km, about 3 times, leaves out the 24 hours
video_script.design: A long road line carries the walk. The walking rates are written in a chain on the working area, each step building on the one before.
open_questions: The 25 km a day, 5 km an hour and 70 years are assumptions taken from the worklist; the book leaves them to the learner.

<bookmark mark='assume'/>Assume the group walked twenty five kilometres in a day, and divide.
<bookmark mark='hundred'/>Twenty five times four is one hundred, and four hundred is four hundreds.

narration: <bookmark mark='s2'/>Step two, the lifetime walk. Assume five kilometres in each hour, day and night.
<bookmark mark='day'/>In one day, that is five times twenty four, which is one hundred twenty kilometres.
<bookmark mark='year'/>For one year, multiply by three hundred sixty five.
That is forty three thousand eight hundred kilometres.

narration: <bookmark mark='s3'/>Step three, a lifetime is seventy years.
<bookmark mark='seven'/>Forty three thousand eight hundred times seven is three hundred six thousand six hundred.
<bookmark mark='ten'/>Times ten more gives three million sixty six thousand kilometres.

narration: <bookmark mark='s4'/>Step four, divide by the distance around the Earth.
<bookmark mark='cancel'/>Three million sixty six thousand divided by forty thousand. Cancel four zeroes from both.
That leaves three hundred six point six divided by four.

beats.on_screen: 400 ÷ 25 = 4 × 4 = 16 days; 306.6 ÷ 4 = 76.65, about 76 times around the Earth

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>State each assumption, then multiply the rates one step at a time.
<bookmark mark='ans1'/>Four times four is sixteen, so the group started about sixteen days ago.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>Three hundred six point six divided by four is seventy six point six five.
That is about seventy six times around the Earth.
